seoTitle: How to Permanently Delete a Google Workspace Account
metaDescription: Step-by-step guide to permanently deleting your Google Workspace account, including canceling billing and understanding what deletion actually removes.
intro: Permanently deleting a Google Workspace account removes every user, every email, and every Drive file tied to it, so it's a step worth taking carefully whether you're closing a business or switching platforms. The Admin console spreads the process across a few different sections — billing, account settings, and the account management panel itself — which is where most people get stuck looking for a single "delete" button. This guide walks through the actual path: signing into the Admin console, handling billing first, and finding where account deletion really lives.

steps.heading: Back up anything you need before you start
steps.body: Deletion in Google Workspace is irreversible once it completes, so before touching any settings, export or download the emails, Drive files, and contacts you or your team might need later. Google Takeout can pull a full copy of most Workspace data if you haven't already been backing up separately — treat this as the one step in the whole process you can't undo your way out of.

steps.heading: Sign in and open the Admin console
steps.body: From any Google page, open the app grid in the top right and choose Admin — this is the console every account-level setting, including billing and deletion, lives inside. You need to be signed in with an account that has admin rights on the Workspace domain; a regular user account won't have access to account management at all.

image.caption: The Google app grid with Admin highlighted. Account deletion only becomes accessible once you're inside the Admin console with an admin-level account.

steps.heading: Cancel your subscription first
steps.body: From the Admin console home, find the Billing card under Manage Workspace, which shows your paid service start date and links to Manage subscriptions, Payment accounts, and Buy or upgrade. Cancel the active subscription here before attempting deletion — Google generally won't let the account closure process complete cleanly while a paid subscription is still running, and skipping this step is one of the most common causes of a failed deletion later.

image.caption: The Admin console home screen, with the Billing card showing subscription details and links to manage or cancel it — this needs handling before deletion will go through.

steps.heading: Remove any domains attached to the account
steps.body: Still in the Admin console, go to Account, then Domains, and detach or remove any domains connected to the Workspace account. A domain still tied to an active Workspace account is another common blocker for a clean deletion, since Google treats domain association as something that needs resolving before the account itself can be closed.

steps.heading: Find the account deletion option
steps.body: Go to Account, then Account settings, and scroll to Account management. This section states plainly what deletion does — permanently deleting the account removes all user accounts, their data, and access to every connected service — and it's the actual entry point for closing the account, not something tucked into Billing or Security. Read this warning fully before proceeding, since it's your last confirmation of exactly what's about to be erased.

image.caption: The Account management section under Account settings, stating that deleting the account will permanently remove all user accounts, their data, and access to services.

steps.heading: Watch for common deletion errors
steps.body: If the deletion process fails partway through, it's almost always one of the things covered above: an active subscription that wasn't fully canceled, a domain that's still attached, or a pending payment that hasn't cleared. Resolve whichever one the error message points to and retry — the process itself typically finishes within minutes to a few hours once billing, domains, and services are all properly cleared.

faq.question: Can I recover my Google Workspace account after permanent deletion?
faq.answer: No, once the deletion process fully completes, the account and its data cannot be recovered, which is why backing up everything beforehand is essential.

faq.question: Do I need to cancel my subscription before deleting the account?
faq.answer: Yes, canceling your subscription under Billing → Manage subscriptions is typically a required first step before the Admin console will let deletion proceed cleanly.

faq.question: Why might my Google Workspace deletion fail?
faq.answer: Deletion commonly fails due to an active subscription, an unresolved payment, or a domain still attached to the account — clear each of these first.

faq.question: How long does it take to permanently delete a Workspace account?
faq.answer: The process can take anywhere from a few minutes to several hours depending on how quickly billing, domains, and related services are resolved beforehand.

faq.question: Where exactly do I go to delete the account?
faq.answer: Account → Account settings → Account management inside the Admin console — this section explains what deletion removes and is the actual entry point for closing the account.
